_comment: The resource policy on the AWS Secrets Manager secret. scripts/setup.sh drops this
_comment key, fills in <POD_ROLE_ARN> with the pod's dedicated EKS Pod Identity role
and calls secretsmanager:PutResourcePolicy with the result.
This is the only grant the role has on the secret, because the role carries no
resource policy on its own is enough to authorize a principal in the same account
(AWS Secrets Manager User Guide, 'Permissions policies attached to an AWS Secrets
What it deliberately does not grant:
* no secretsmanager:PutSecretValue or UpdateSecret, so the workload cannot replace
the ciphertext with one wrapped under a key it chose;
* nothing on AWS KMS. Reading this secret decrypts it at rest with the AWS managed
key aws/secretsmanager, which the service does on the caller's behalf; the
sample's own key, the one holding the secret's value, is reached only through the
conditional allow in the key policy, where the attestation condition sits.
